name: Quest placement accuracy over labelled messages, balanced with cost and time
purpose: Measures whether a message is placed on exactly the quests it is about, or on none when no quest fits. Read in this direction: maximise the share of messages placed on exactly the labelled quests (none included) while a placement stays within its cost and time budgets. One number at every stage: accuracy, cost and time at the weights and budgets of [balance.place_on_a_quest], fixed before any arm was scored; an arm that spends the whole of a budget gets zero for it, so a model call has to buy its price in accuracy, and the library's judge, which sees only the quests in the order given, pays for that in accuracy on a large account. Case sources of the one number (none a stage, none with a pass test of its own): named quests, topics implied without the quest's words, vague cues resolved only by a milestone phrase, distractors that share words with the wrong quest, messages no quest fits, messages about two quests, and follow-ups that name nothing; plus real labelled messages where a machine holds them (QAR_PRIVATE_PLACEMENT_DATASET, at the share fixed in esoi.toml, absent means no case). The account is invented, a long list of quests of which a few are the ones the cases are about, with no Spiritual Data name.
record: Per implementation on the same cases: the exact-match rate, the right quest within the first three candidates, model calls, dollars and seconds per case, and the balanced number; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. Idea ratings of the descriptions (0 to 4 on the five questions of esoi/idea-rating-scale.md): shared-quest-ranker 3,3,3,4,4 (an embedding of the title alone cannot see milestones); hybrid-candidate-ranker 4,4,3,2,4 (costs an index read); library-quest-judge 2,2,3,4,4 (sees only the first quests it is given). The results are in evaluation/components/results.csv and the leaderboard of the cascade. The account-replay stage is the production function on real data: quest-backend scripts/checks/quest_placement_replay.py runs select_and_rank_quests_for_text over one person's hand-created tasks of the last N days (the label is the quest each task sits on), with every database and vector write blocked, and prints per case and in a summary the exact match of the pick, the judge's own exact pick, the label within the first three, the judge's abstentions and the wrong picks that cross a team or an organization; its --arm overlay runs the repository's own placement code in-process on a deployed image before a release (the quest embeddings, and the earlier placed items a case may learn from, computed in memory; for each case only items placed strictly before it count, a temporal split) and --task-ids restricts the cases to a labelled set. Public cases may carry optional examples (earlier placed items); the example-vote arms read them. Its rows and case text are kept in a private folder outside every repository, never in evaluation/components/results.csv.
disadvantages: The first stage uses a local embedding model (bge-small) in place of the production embedding service, so its absolute numbers describe the ranking's shape, not production's. The public account is small and invented and the two model arms tie within noise, so the selection is a best guess, not significant; more cases with near-duplicate quests are the next thing to add. The index read the hybrid ranking needs per placement is not in the fixtures' time. The public quests carry no vision statement or purpose, so the fields that say what a quest is for are measured only on real cases and the account replay. The fixtures stand in for the database, so what the real data adds (notes, goals, entries) is only measured on the real source.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > free [sample=full | real=no | gate=competitive | when=the hybrid_candidate_ranker and shared_quest_ranker first-stage arms of place_on_a_quest run the whole case set with no model call, proving the cases and the scorer before any model is paid for] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a single real case runs end to end through a model arm on the Claude Code subscription and is hand-read] > three [sample=sample:3 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=three cases of different sources run through the model arms on the Claude Code subscription and are hand-read] > ten [sample=sample:10 | real=yes | gate=competitive | when=the model arms agree with the labels on ten cases, always with --max-calls] > whole [sample=full | real=yes | gate=competitive | max-age-days=90 | when=a person approved the spend under the metric run policy; the subscription route costs no API dollars] > account-replay [sample=full | real=yes | max-age-days=30 | when=a change to the placement's inputs or prompt is about to ship: the production function itself (quest-backend select_and_rank_quests_for_text) replays one consenting person's own hand-created tasks on the server, read-only, the deployed arm against the candidate arm patched in-process, and its rows stay in a private folder outside every repository]
